principles.text: Setting a stop tighter than the actual structural low (entry candle low) to chase a smaller risk is a tradeoff: you accept getting shaken out more easily; sometimes it still saves risk, sometimes it costs you the trade.
Constantly watching the market even on weekends and vacations is unhealthy and unsustainable; deliberately stepping away and letting stops work for you also helps you hold positions longer.
Be more selective adding new names once the watch list is already large; the marginal value of each additional stock shrinks.
Buy near the daily/weekly EMAs where you can define tight risk; avoid chasing extended names far above the EMAs and avoid buying gap-ups, especially gap-ups after a short squeeze.
Tight stops let you allocate large position size (25-30% of account) while risking only a small fraction (0.25% or less) of the account.
Risk per trade varies only slightly with setup quality (e.g. 0.2% for a B setup vs 0.25% baseline); never half or double size based on conviction alone.
Size off realized equity, not unrealized profits; when doubling the account, only count about half the unrealized gains when computing new risk and position size.
When a leading sector (e.g. semis) has already run for weeks, success rate on new entries drops as they go sideways; don't be aggressive chasing late.
